text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Petroleum minister assures the public that regular fuel supplies will be restored by the weekend. He said a dispute between state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation and the Nigerian Ports Authority, which contributed to the scarcity, would soon be resolved.
- Federal government says the contract for the troubled Ajaokuta steel complex has not been cancelled.
- A national health insurance scheme which was suggested 12 years ago may now take off before June, reliable sources disclose.

- Presidency sources say head of state General Sani Abacha changed his mind about selling off a large part of government's share in crude oil production only 10 days before the annual budget broadcast.
- Absence of details of new government policy on insurance stalled a hearing on Monday over who will take the NNPC account.
- Internal air transport has been paralysed in some parts of the country for almost two weeks by a lack of aviation fuel.
- A deadline of one month has been given to owners of 40 dilapidated vessels to remove them from various seaports or have them sold by the NPA.
